1. SYNOPSIS > 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows:

a) Total GA area ≥2.0 and ≤ 20.5 mm2 (1 to 8 disk areas [DA], respectively)

b) If GA is multifocal, at least one lesion must be ≥1.25 mm 2(0.5 DA), with the overall aggregate area of GA as specified above in 4.a

c) The entire GA lesion must be completely visualized on the macula-centered image and must be able to be imaged in its entirety, and not contiguous with any areas of peripapillary atrophy.

5. GA lesion within foveal and perifoveal region.

6. Sufficient ocular media clarity, pupillary dilation, and subject cooperation to permit acquisition of good quality retinal imaging.

7. Subjects with liver enzyme level ≤ 1.5 x ULN.

8. Presence of any pattern of hyper-autofluorescence in the junctional zone of GA.

9. Subjects who had prior treatment with an approved drug for AMD, e.g. Izervay® (Avacincaptad pegol) or Syfovre® (Pegcetacoplan injection) can be included, after a washout period of at least 3 months in study eye. Subjects can receive an approved drug for AMD in the fellow eye, if required.

10. Subjects with history of participation in another interventional clinical study, use of any experimental treatment for AMD or any other investigational new drug, can be included after a wash out period of 3 months.

1. SYNOPSIS > Study Design and Methodology:

Phase 1 is a multicenter, open-label, dose-ranging/dose-escalating study that will enroll up to 18 subjects.

A 3+3 design will be used for sequential dose-escalation cohorts in which subjects will receive a single subretinal injection of OCU410 in the study eye on Day 1.

1. SYNOPSIS > 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows: > Exclusion Criteria:

1. Previous treatment with a gene-therapy or cell therapy product

2. GA due to causes other than AMD such as Stargardt disease, cone rod dystrophy or toxic maculopathies like Plaquenil maculopathy. However, benign conditions of the vitreous or peripheral retina are not exclusionary (i.e., pavingstone degeneration).

3. Spherical equivalent of the refractive error demonstrating > 6 diopters of myopia or an axial length >26 mm, inability to fixate, uncontrolled glaucoma, advanced cataract, corneal abnormalities, medium haze, and other retinal pathologies.

4. Any history or current evidence of exudative ("wet") AMD including any evidence of retinal pigment epithelium rips, branch retinal artery or vein occlusion, corneal transplant, or evidence of neovascularization anywhere in the retina based on fluorescein angiogram.

1. SYNOPSIS > 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

1. If none of the first 3 subjects on medium dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), then the dose will be escalated to high dose concentration for the next cohort.

2. If 2 or more of the first 3 subjects on medium dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

3. If exactly 1 of the first 3 subjects on medium dose concentration is determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then 3 additional subjects will be enrolled on medium dose concentration.

a) If none of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be escalated to high dose concentration for the next cohort.

b) If 1 or more of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

Cohort 3 High Dose (1.5x1011vg/mL): 3 subjects will receive a subretinal injection of 200 ul of OCU410 high dose concentration.

The DSMB will review two weeks safety data after dosing the first subject in cohort 3. If there are no dose-limiting toxicities observed, Phase 2 dosing will begin simultaneously with subsequent subjects in Cohort 3. In the event of a DLT, the algorithm of DLT (de-escalation or addition of 3 subjects) will be followed.

1. If none of the first 3 subjects on high dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the high dose will be determined to be the maximum tolerated dose (MTD).

2. If 2 or more of the first 3 subjects on high dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

3. If exactly 1 of the first 3 subjects on high dose concentration is determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then 3 additional subjects will be enrolled on high dose concentration.

a) If none of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the high dose will be determined to be the MTD.

b) If 1 or more of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

The DSMB will provide recommendations on proceeding to Phase 2 study at either the targeted dose, proceeding at an adjusted dose, increasing the cohort size, adding a cohort, or stopping further cohort administration if stopping criteria/criterion have been met.

The DSMB will continue to review the safety data for all enrolled subjects at the completion of the 3- month, 6-month, 9-month, and 12-month visits.

Under this design, there will be 9 subjects enrolled if there are no DLTs and up to 18 subjects under the condition that exactly 1 of the 3 subjects of every cohort is determined to have a DLT.

1. SYNOPSIS > The following algorithm will be followed for dose-escalation Phase 1 study:

Cohort 1 Low Dose (2.5x1010 vg/mL): 3 subjects will receive a subretinal injection 200 uL of OCU410 low dose concentration. The Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will review 2 weeks of safety data post-dosing and if none of the 3 subjects on low dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), then the dose will be escalated to medium dose concentration for the next cohort. In the event of a DLT, the algorithm of DLT (de-escalation or addition of 3 subjects) will be followed.

The Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will also review 4 weeks of safety data post-dosing. 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects:

1. If none of the first 3 subjects on low dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), then the dose will be escalated to medium dose concentration for the next cohort.

2. If 2 or more of the first 3 subjects on low dose concentration are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

3. If exactly 1 of the first 3 subjects on low dose concentration is determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then 3 additional subjects will be enrolled on low dose concentration.

a) If none of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be escalated to medium dose concentration for the next cohort.

b) If 1 or more of the 3 additional subjects are determined by the DSMB to have a DLT, then the dose will be de-escalated for the next cohort.

Cohort 2 Medium Dose (5×1010 vg/mL): 3 subjects will receive a subretinal injection 200 uL of OCU410 medium dose concentration. The Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will review 4 weeks of safety data post-dosing.

Phase 2 is a randomized dose-expansion cohort in which subjects will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive either the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) from Phase 1, or to receive a lower dose to be determined based on the safety profile from Phase 1, or to an untreated control group. A total of up to 51 subjects will be enrolled in the dose-expansion phase.

In the dose-expansion phase of the study, subjects will be randomized 1:1:1 to either two OCU410 dose groups (n=17 per group) or to an untreated control group (n=17).

Subjects who are enrolled in the untreated control group of the study will not receive any treatment. They will be followed according to the same treatment schedule as the treated subjects.

1. SYNOPSIS > 1 of 3 results will occur from the 3 subjects: > 4. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging shows:

a) Total GA area ≥2.0 and ≤ 20.5 mm2 (1 to 8 disk areas [DA], respectively)

b) If GA is multifocal, at least one lesion must be ≥1.25 mm 2 (0.5 DA), with the overall aggregate area of GA as specified above in 4.a

c) The entire GA lesion must be completely visualized on the macula-centered image and must be able to be imaged in its entirety, and not contiguous with any areas of peripapillary atrophy.

5. GA lesion within foveal and perifoveal region.

6. Sufficient ocular media clarity, pupillary dilation, and subject cooperation to permit acquisition of good quality retinal imaging.

7. Subjects with liver enzyme level ≤ 1.5 x ULN.

8. Presence of any pattern of hyper-autofluorescence in the junctional zone of GA.

9. Subjects who had prior treatment with an approved drug for AMD, e.g. Izervay® (Avacincaptad pegol) or Syfovre® (Pegcetacoplan injection) can be included, after a washout period of at least 3 months in study eye. Subjects can receive an approved drug for AMD in the fellow eye, if required.

10. Subjects with history of participation in another interventional clinical study, use of any experimental treatment for AMD or any other investigational new drug, can be included after a wash out period of 3 months.

Note: Subject inclusion will be determined by Sponsor upon reviewing subjects screening packet, PI recommendations and in consultation with scientific advisory board (SAB). Dosing eye recommendations for surgery will be made by PI and study surgeon by reviewing screening packet and on a case-by-case basis. This recommendation will be approved by the Sponsor. Dosing eye determination can be made prior or on the day of the surgery, by evaluating the latest Ophthalmic examinations, medical history, FAF and SD-OCT images.
